method: ffprobe; ffmpeg contact sheets fps=2 (4 sheets, all viewed); scene detect gt(scene,0.3) found 0 hard cuts: the film is one continuous camera flight joined by whip pans, so shot changes were placed from the sheets; dense fps=15 sheets at 2.0–3.6 s (first whip) and 19.6–21.2 s (logo flash and pull-back). Audio present but not analysed: whether whips land on music beats is unverified

visual_language: 3D-rendered toy-like world (glossy plastic, chrome, coiled cables) floating in a saturated cobalt-to-white sky, shot with shallow depth of field and heavy motion blur. There are no hard cuts: one continuous camera flies between objects that hang around a central pole, joined by whip pans of about 0.4–0.45 s (ease-in-out, blur peak mid-move, small overshoot settle of about 0.5 s), often with a nearby object passing as a foreground wipe. All text lives on in-world LED screens in dot-matrix letters (white for statements, amber for labels and tiles, one orange key word), typed letter by letter with a cursor or scrolled like a ticker; never as flat overlay type. Rhythm is fast: 10 shots in 24 s (about 2.4 s each), with a whip roughly every 2.5–3 s, and a longer 4 s hold for the payoff line. Palette: cobalt blue, orange accent, cream plastic, black screens, small purple, green and red props. Signature moments: the hero object's own screen typing the opening line, the speech-bubble sign as the home for statements, tiles flipping in to spell the key word, the white screen flash, and the pull-back end card that brings the opening hero back. Format is 16:9; the vertical pole composition reframes naturally to 9:16.
continuity: The speech-bubble LED sign on the pole is home: visited three times (r2-s2, r2-s8, r2-s9) and always where the main statement is typed.
The hero radio bookends the film: extreme close-up at the start (r2-s1), whole and hanging in the end card (r2-s10).
One text medium throughout: dot-matrix LED letters on the radio display, the sign, the ticker and the tiles.
The letter tiles that spell the key word (r2-s7) return in the end card (r2-s10).
Cables and the central pole physically connect every object, so the camera travels along them from one shot to the next.
Whips use a nearby object (radio body, black panel, cassette) as the wipe, so the world never cuts.
Small floating props (squiggles, capsules) persist as parallax layers in every shot and keep the space continuous.
look: Real 3D (not flat, not 2.5D): toy-like objects with rounded bevelled edges; glossy plastic bodies with soft specular highlights, chrome rings and poles, matte black emissive LED screens; soft studio key light from upper left plus a bright sky fill, soft contact shadows and ambient occlusion where objects meet; shallow depth of field (background props blurred), heavy directional motion blur on whips; background is an open sky gradient with soft haze, no ground plane.
code_translation: Not code-native (3D render). Per D55 (2026-11-02) it is built as real 3D in code with three.js: bevelled/rounded geometry, MeshPhysicalMaterial for glossy plastic (clearcoat) and chrome (metalness), emissive canvas textures for LED screens, one soft key light with soft shadows plus hemisphere sky fill, depth of field as a blur pass (or layered blur), whips as a fast camera rotation with directional motion blur, sky as a large gradient backdrop with haze. Never flattened into 2D shapes. Persian LED text must be rendered from the shaped brand font onto a canvas and then dotted, never with a Latin pixel font, so letters stay joined.

risks: Third-party film of unknown origin: ADAPT only. Never copy the object designs, the copy, the 'LOUD ONE' logo or the shot order one by one.
16:9 source, 9:16 films: compositions must be reframed vertically, with the pole/sign stack centred inside the safe zone.
Heavy motion blur and fast whips (about every 2.5 s) must still respect minimum hold times for Persian text; readability wins over pace.
Dot-matrix effect on Persian text can hurt legibility at small sizes; keep dots fine and text large.
Reference colours (cobalt, orange) map onto brand colour roles: sky = background role, hero body = primary role, key word = accent role; never used as literal hex values.
